summary: Well‑documented, preregistered paired emulation study of a generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline for LLM‑generated network configs. Execution artifacts show every paired episode was scored safe under both arms (n=240 pairs), producing a degenerate paired contrast (risk difference = 0.00, 95% CI [0.00,0.00], McNemar p=1.0). The manuscript correctly attributes the null result to the preregistered shared_initial_candidate contract (one shared initial LLM generation per pair) and zero validator repairs. Strong archival provenance and reproducibility artifacts are present, but the manuscript currently includes excessive run-level provenance (file paths and full hashes) and an overly verbose Disclosure Statement that duplicates execution logs. Required manuscript edits are limited to presentation/formatting and disclosure condensation; substantive scientific claims are appropriately bounded and supported by the archived artifacts.
critical_issues: Manuscript includes extensive run‑internal file paths and full artifact hashes in the main text and Results/Methods, violating the track instruction that ordinary scientific prose must not duplicate audit logs; only the single mandatory master_prompt locator+SHA‑256 may appear in the Disclosure Statement.

Disclosure Statement duplicates execution accounting and per‑call provenance already preserved in the archive; it must be condensed to a concise statement that reports models, validator, adapter contract, preregistration locator+SHA, human/autonomy boundary, and the single required master_prompt locator+SHA, without reprinting execution logs, per‑file hashes, or per‑file paths.

References/inline claims: while cited records appear to exist in the provided bibliographic records, verify that every numbered in‑text citation precisely supports the nearby claim (no unverifiable or overbroad citation claims). If any reference used only as an identifier (arXiv/DOI) can be replaced by a conventional IEEE bibliographic entry from the archived metadata, do so.
required_revisions: Remove all run‑internal file paths and full SHA‑256 digests from the main manuscript text (Methods, Results, Figures, Tables) and move them to the archived execution bundle; preserve exactly one immutable master_prompt locator+SHA‑256 in the Disclosure Statement as required.

Condense the Disclosure Statement to a concise paragraph that lists: LLM(s) and declared model id, adapter/orchestration family and validator id, preregistration id+SHA‑256, the single archived master_prompt path+SHA‑256 (mandatory), the human/autonomy boundary summary, and a short pointer to the archived execution manifest (no per‑file paths or hashes). Do not duplicate execution logs or per‑call trace details in the Disclosure Statement.

Confirm and, if necessary, replace any identifier‑only reference entries in the References section with full IEEE‑style bibliographic metadata (authors, title, venue or arXiv, year, DOI where available) using the supplied terminal_bibliographic_records; ensure each numbered citation in text is supported by the cited record's content.
optional_revisions: Explicitly state in the Abstract a short qualifier that the primary estimand was uninformative under the used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sentence), to improve reader expectations at first glance.

Shorten or relocate long example JSON snippets, validator trace excerpts, and representative artifact excerpts from main text into a compact appendix within the five pages if needed, or reference them only by archive pointer (but do not reprint full hashes/paths).

Add a one‑paragraph checklist in Methods mapping preregistered analysis items to archived file names (high‑level, not per‑file hashes), to make traceability easier for readers without reproducing low‑level provenance in prose.
